sanskrit: hayaughāś ca rathaughāś ca tatra tatra viśāṃ pate saṃpatantaḥ sma dṛśyante nighnamānāḥ parasparam
english: Floods of horses and floods of chariots, O lord of peoples, were seen rushing together here and there, striking one another down.

sanskrit: dhāvatāṃ ca rathaughānāṃ nighnatāṃ ca pṛthak pṛthak babhūva tumulaḥ śabdo vimiśro dundubhisvanaiḥ
english: From the streaming masses of chariots, racing onward and striking down each its own foe, there arose a tumultuous din mingled with the booming of war-drums.

sanskrit: divaspṛṅ naravīrāṇāṃ nighnatām itaretaram saṃprahāre sutumule tava teṣāṃ ca bhārata
english: In that exceedingly tumultuous clash, O Bhārata, as the heroic men slew one another—yours and theirs alike—the uproar touched the very heavens.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato vyūḍheṣv anīkeṣu tāvakeṣv itareṣu ca dhanaṃjayo rathānīkam avadhīt tava bhārata śarair atiratho yuddhe pātayan rathayūthapān
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, when the armies were arrayed—both yours and the others'—Dhanaṃjaya, that surpassing chariot-warrior, smote your host of chariots, O Bhārata, felling the leaders of chariot-bands with his arrows in the battle.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ pārthena kāleneva yugakṣaye dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe yattāḥ pāṇḍavān pratyayodhayan prārthayānā yaśo dīptaṃ mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam
english: Slaughtered by Pārtha as though by Time itself at the dissolution of an age, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, straining hard in the fight, battled back against the Pāṇḍavas, seeking blazing glory and making death their only retreat.

sanskrit: ekāgramanaso bhūtvā pāṇḍavānāṃ varūthinīm babhañjur bahuśo rājaṃs te cābhajyanta saṃyuge
english: With single-minded resolve they shattered the Pāṇḍava host again and again, O king, and were themselves shattered in turn in the combat.

sanskrit: dravadbhir atha bhagnaiś ca parivartadbhir eva ca pāṇḍavaiḥ kauravaiś caiva na prajñāyata kiṃ cana
english: With the Pāṇḍavas and the Kauravas now fleeing, now broken, now wheeling about to charge again, nothing whatever could be made out.

sanskrit: udatiṣṭhad rajo bhaumaṃ chādayānaṃ divākaram diśaḥ pratidiśo vāpi tatra jajñuḥ kathaṃ cana
english: A dust rose up from the earth that veiled the sun, and there none could in any way distinguish the quarters or the intermediate quarters of the sky.

sanskrit: anumānena saṃjñābhir nāmagotraiś ca saṃyuge vartate sma tadā yuddhaṃ tatra tatra viśāṃ pate
english: By guesswork, by watchwords, and by names and lineages the fighting was carried on then, here and there, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: na vyūho bhidyate tatra kauravāṇāṃ kathaṃ cana rakṣitaḥ satyasaṃdhena bhāradvājena dhīmatā
english: There the battle-array of the Kauravas could in no way be broken, guarded as it was by the wise Bhāradvāja, true to his word.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍaveyānāṃ rakṣitaḥ savyasācinā nābhidhyata mahāvyūho bhīmena ca surakṣitaḥ
english: In like manner the great array of the Pāṇḍavas, guarded by Savyasācin and well protected by Bhīma, could not be pierced.

sanskrit: senāgrād abhiniṣpatya prāyudhyaṃs tatra mānavāḥ ubhayoḥ senayo rājan vyatiṣaktarathadvipāḥ
english: Sallying forth from the front of the host, the men fought there, O king, the chariots and elephants of both armies locked together in the fray.

sanskrit: hayārohair hayārohāḥ pātyante sma mahāhave ṛṣṭibhir vimalāgrābhiḥ prāsair api ca saṃyuge
english: In that great battle horsemen were brought down by horsemen with bright-pointed lances and with javelins in the fight.

sanskrit: rathī rathinam āsādya śaraiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ pātayām āsa samare tasminn atibhayaṃkare
english: Closing with a chariot-warrior, a chariot-warrior felled him with gold-adorned arrows in that exceedingly terrible battle.

sanskrit: gajārohā gajārohān nārācaśaratomaraiḥ saṃsaktāḥ pātayām āsus tava teṣāṃ ca saṃghaśaḥ
english: Elephant-riders, locked in combat, brought down elephant-riders in companies—yours and theirs alike—with iron shafts, arrows, and lances.

sanskrit: pattisaṃghā raṇe pattīn bhiṇḍipālaparaśvadhaiḥ nyapātayanta saṃhṛṣṭāḥ parasparakṛtāgasaḥ
english: Bands of foot-soldiers in the fray, exhilarated and bearing mutual wrongs, struck down foot-soldiers with slings and battle-axes.

sanskrit: padātī rathinaṃ saṃkhye rathī cāpi padātinam nyapātayac chitaiḥ śastraiḥ senayor ubhayor api
english: In the encounter a foot-soldier felled a chariot-warrior, and a chariot-warrior too a foot-soldier, with sharpened weapons, on both sides alike.

sanskrit: gajārohā hayārohān pātayāṃ cakrire tadā hayārohā gajasthāṃś ca tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Elephant-riders then brought down horsemen, and horsemen those mounted on elephants; and this seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: gajārohavaraiś cāpi tatra tatra padātayaḥ pātitāḥ samadṛśyanta taiś cāpi gajayodhinaḥ
english: By foremost elephant-riders foot-soldiers were seen struck down here and there, and by those foot-soldiers in turn the elephant-warriors.

sanskrit: pattisaṃghā hayārohaiḥ sādisaṃghāś ca pattibhiḥ pātyamānā vyadṛśyanta śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Bands of foot-soldiers being felled by horsemen, and bands of cavalry by foot-soldiers, were seen by the hundreds and by the thousands.

sanskrit: dhvajais tatrāpaviddhaiś ca kārmukais tomarais tathā prāsais tathā gadābhiś ca parighaiḥ kampanais tathā
english: With banners cast down there, with bows and lances, with javelins and maces, with iron clubs and tremor-shafts,

sanskrit: śaktibhiḥ kavacaiś citraiḥ kaṇapair aṅkuśair api nistriṃśair vimalaiś cāpi svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ śarais tathā
english: with spears and gleaming variegated coats of mail, with barbed darts and goads, with bright swords, and with gold-feathered arrows,

sanskrit: paristomaiḥ kuthābhiś ca kambalaiś ca mahādhanaiḥ bhūr bhāti bharataśreṣṭha sragdāmair iva citritā
english: with horse-cloths and elephant-housings and costly blankets, the earth shone, O best of the Bharatas, as though figured all over with wreaths and garlands.

sanskrit: narāśvakāyaiḥ patitair dantibhiś ca mahāhave agamyarūpā pṛthivī māṃsaśoṇitakardamā
english: With the fallen bodies of men and horses, and with elephants, in that great battle the earth became impassable, miry with flesh and blood.

sanskrit: praśaśāma rajo bhaumaṃ vyukṣitaṃ raṇaśoṇitaiḥ diśaś ca vimalāḥ sarvāḥ saṃbabhūvur janeśvara
english: The dust of the earth, drenched with the blood of battle, settled, and all the quarters became clear, O lord of men.

sanskrit: utthitāny agaṇeyāni kabandhāni samantataḥ cihnabhūtāni jagato vināśārthāya bhārata
english: Headless trunks beyond counting rose up on every side, become as it were portents foretelling the destruction of the world, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tasmin yuddhe mahāraudre vartamāne sudāruṇe pratyadṛśyanta rathino dhāvamānāḥ samantataḥ
english: As that most fearsome and dreadful battle was raging, chariot-warriors were seen racing about on every side.

sanskrit: tato droṇaś ca bhīṣmaś ca saindhavaś ca jayadrathaḥ purumitro vikarṇaś ca śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ
english: Then Droṇa and Bhīṣma, and Jayadratha lord of the Sindhus, Purumitra and Vikarṇa, and Śakuni son of Subala—

sanskrit: ete samaradurdharṣāḥ siṃhatulyaparākramāḥ pāṇḍavānām anīkāni babhañjuḥ sma punaḥ punaḥ
english: these, unassailable in battle and lion-like in prowess, shattered the ranks of the Pāṇḍavas again and again.

sanskrit: tathaiva bhīmaseno 'pi rākṣasaś ca ghaṭotkacaḥ sātyakiś cekitānaś ca draupadeyāś ca bhārata
english: In like manner Bhīmasena too, and the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca, Sātyaki and Cekitāna, and the sons of Draupadī, O Bhārata,

sanskrit: tāvakāṃs tava putrāṃś ca sahitān sarvarājabhiḥ drāvayām āsur ājau te tridaśā dānavān iva
english: drove your men and your sons, together with all the kings, in flight upon the field, as the thirty gods rout the dānavas.

sanskrit: tathā te samare 'nyonyaṃ nighnantaḥ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ raktokṣitā ghorarūpā virejur dānavā iva
english: Thus those bulls among warriors, slaying one another in the fight, drenched with blood and dreadful of aspect, shone like dānavas.

sanskrit: vinirjitya ripūn vīrāḥ senayor ubhayor api vyadṛśyanta mahāmātrā grahā iva nabhastale
english: Having vanquished their foes, the heroic high officers of both armies were seen like planets in the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: tato rathasahasreṇa putro duryodhanas tava abhyayāt pāṇḍavān yuddhe rākṣasaṃ ca ghaṭotkacam
english: Then your son Duryodhana, with a thousand chariots, advanced upon the Pāṇḍavas in battle and upon the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavāḥ sarve mahatyā senayā saha droṇabhīṣmau raṇe śūrau pratyudyayur ariṃdamau
english: In like manner all the Pāṇḍavas, with a mighty host, advanced to meet the valiant, foe-subduing Droṇa and Bhīṣma in the battle.

sanskrit: kirīṭī tu yayau kruddhaḥ samarthān pārthivottamān ārjuniḥ sātyakiś caiva yayatuḥ saubalaṃ balam
english: The Diademed One, enraged, advanced against the most capable of kings, while the son of Arjuna and Sātyaki advanced against the host of Subala's son.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte bhūyaḥ saṃgrāmo lomaharṣaṇaḥ tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca samare vijigīṣatām
english: Then once more there arose a hair-raising combat between your men and the foe, each striving for victory in the fight.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tatas te pārthivāḥ kruddhāḥ phalgunaṃ vīkṣya saṃyuge rathair anekasāhasraiḥ samantāt paryavārayan
english: Saṃjaya said: Then those kings, enraged at the sight of Phalguna in the battle, surrounded him on every side with many thousands of chariots.

sanskrit: athainaṃ rathavṛndena koṣṭakīkṛtya bhārata śaraiḥ subahusāhasraiḥ samantād abhyavārayan
english: And having penned him in, O Bhārata, within a ring of chariots, they hemmed him about on every side with many thousands of arrows.

sanskrit: śaktīś ca vimalās tīkṣṇā gadāś ca parighaiḥ saha prāsān paraśvadhāṃś caiva mudgarān musalān api cikṣipuḥ samare kruddhāḥ phalgunasya rathaṃ prati
english: Bright sharp spears, maces and iron bludgeons, javelins and battle-axes, mallets and pestles too—enraged, they hurled them all in the battle against the chariot of Phalguna.

sanskrit: śastrāṇām atha tāṃ vṛṣṭiṃ śalabhānām ivāyatim rurodha sarvataḥ pārthaḥ śaraiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ
english: That downpour of weapons, sweeping on like a swarm of locusts, Pārtha checked on every side with his gold-adorned arrows.

sanskrit: tatra tal lāghavaṃ dṛṣṭvā bībhatsor atimānuṣam devadānavagandharvāḥ piśācoragarākṣasāḥ sādhu sādhv iti rājendra phalgunaṃ pratyapūjayan
english: Beholding there that more-than-human dexterity of Bībhatsu, the gods, dānavas, and gandharvas, the piśācas, serpents, and rākṣasas honored Phalguna, O lord of kings, crying 'Well done! Well done!'

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ cābhimanyuṃ ca mahatyā senayā saha gāndhārāḥ samare śūrā rurudhuḥ sahasaubalāḥ
english: And the valiant Gāndhāras, together with the sons of Subala, with a great host beset Sātyaki and Abhimanyu in the battle.

sanskrit: tatra saubalakāḥ kruddhā vārṣṇeyasya rathottamam tilaśaś cicchiduḥ krodhāc chastrair nānāvidhair yudhi
english: There the enraged followers of Subala's son, in their wrath, cut the splendid chariot of the Vārṣṇeya to bits in the fight with weapons of every kind.

sanskrit: sātyakis tu rathaṃ tyaktvā vartamāne mahābhaye abhimanyo rathaṃ tūrṇam āruroha paraṃtapaḥ
english: But Sātyaki, scorcher of foes, abandoning his chariot amid that great peril, swiftly mounted the chariot of Abhimanyu.

sanskrit: tāv ekarathasaṃyuktau saubaleyasya vāhinīm vyadhametāṃ śitais tūrṇaṃ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: The two of them, joined upon a single chariot, swiftly shattered the host of Subala's son with sharp, smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: droṇabhīṣmau raṇe yattau dharmarājasya vāhinīm nāśayetāṃ śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ kaṅkapatraparicchadaiḥ
english: Droṇa and Bhīṣma, straining hard in the battle, laid waste the host of the King of Righteousness with keen, heron-feathered arrows.

sanskrit: tato dharmasuto rājā mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau miṣatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ droṇānīkam upādravan
english: Then the royal son of Dharma and the two Pāṇḍava sons of Mādrī, before the eyes of all the troops, charged the array of Droṇa.

sanskrit: tatrāsīt sumahad yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam yathā devāsuraṃ yuddhaṃ pūrvam āsīt sudāruṇam
english: There ensued a vast, tumultuous, hair-raising battle, as dreadful as was of old the war between the gods and the asuras.

sanskrit: kurvāṇau tu mahat karma bhīmasenaghaṭotkacau duryodhanas tato 'bhyetya tāv ubhāv abhyavārayat
english: As Bhīmasena and Ghaṭotkaca were performing mighty deeds, Duryodhana then came up and beset them both.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma haiḍimbasya parākramam atītya pitaraṃ yuddhe yad ayudhyata bhārata
english: There we beheld the marvelous prowess of Hiḍimbā's son, in that he fought in the battle surpassing even his father, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu saṃkruddho duryodhanam amarṣaṇam hṛdy avidhyat pṛṣatkena prahasann iva pāṇḍavaḥ
english: But Bhīmasena, greatly enraged, smote the unforgiving Duryodhana in the breast with a shaft, the Pāṇḍava as it were laughing the while.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā prahāravaramohitaḥ niṣasāda rathopasthe kaśmalaṃ ca jagāma ha
english: Then King Duryodhana, stunned by that grievous blow, sank down upon the floor of his chariot and fell into a swoon.

sanskrit: taṃ visaṃjñam atho jñātvā tvaramāṇo 'sya sārathiḥ apovāha raṇād rājaṃs tataḥ sainyam abhidyata
english: Then his charioteer, perceiving him senseless, in haste bore him away from the battle, O king; and thereupon the army broke apart.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ kauravīṃ senāṃ dravamāṇāṃ samantataḥ nighnan bhīmaḥ śarais tīkṣṇair anuvavrāja pṛṣṭhataḥ
english: Then Bhīma, smiting with keen arrows that Kaurava host as it fled on every side, pursued it from behind.

sanskrit: pārṣataś ca rathaśreṣṭho dharmaputraś ca pāṇḍavaḥ droṇasya paśyataḥ sainyaṃ gāṅgeyasya ca paśyataḥ jaghnatur viśikhais tīkṣṇaiḥ parānīkaviśātanaiḥ
english: And the son of Pṛṣata, foremost of chariot-warriors, and the Pāṇḍava son of Dharma, while Droṇa looked on and the son of Gaṅgā looked on, struck down the host with keen shafts that scatter the ranks of the foe.

sanskrit: dravamāṇaṃ tu tat sainyaṃ tava putrasya saṃyuge nāśaknutāṃ vārayituṃ bhīṣmadroṇau mahārathau
english: That host of your son, fleeing in the battle, the great chariot-warriors Bhīṣma and Droṇa were not able to stay.

sanskrit: vāryamāṇaṃ hi bhīṣmeṇa droṇena ca viśāṃ pate vidravaty eva tat sainyaṃ paśyator droṇabhīṣmayoḥ
english: For though held back by Bhīṣma and by Droṇa, O lord of peoples, that host kept fleeing on, even as Droṇa and Bhīṣma looked on.

sanskrit: tato rathasahasreṣu vidravatsu tatas tataḥ tāv āsthitāv ekarathaṃ saubhadraśinipuṃgavau saubalīṃ samare senāṃ śātayetāṃ samantataḥ
english: Then, as thousands of chariots fled this way and that, the son of Subhadrā and the bull of the Śini line, mounted upon a single chariot, hewed down the host of Subala's son on every side in the battle.

sanskrit: śuśubhāte tadā tau tu śaineyakurupuṃgavau amāvāsyāṃ gatau yadvat somasūryau nabhastale
english: Those two then, the scion of the Śinis and the bull of the Kurus, shone forth like the moon and the sun met together in the sky on the night of the new moon.

sanskrit: arjunas tu tataḥ kruddhas tava sainyaṃ viśāṃ pate vavarṣa śaravarṣeṇa dhārābhir iva toyadaḥ
english: Then Arjuna, enraged, rained upon your host, O lord of peoples, a shower of arrows, as a rain-cloud pours down its streams.

sanskrit: vadhyamānaṃ tatas tat tu śaraiḥ pārthasya saṃyuge dudrāva kauravaṃ sainyaṃ viṣādabhayakampitam
english: Slaughtered by Pārtha's arrows in the battle, the Kaurava host then fled, trembling with despair and terror.

sanskrit: dravatas tān samālokya bhīṣmadroṇau mahārathau nyavārayetāṃ saṃrabdhau duryodhanahitaiṣiṇau
english: Beholding them in flight, the great chariot-warriors Bhīṣma and Droṇa, wrought up and seeking Duryodhana's welfare, sought to stay them.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā samāśvasya viśāṃ pate nyavartayata tat sainyaṃ dravamāṇaṃ samantataḥ
english: Then King Duryodhana, having recovered his senses, O lord of peoples, turned back that host which was fleeing on every side.

sanskrit: yatra yatra sutaṃ tubhyaṃ yo yaḥ paśyati bhārata tatra tatra nyavartanta kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahārathāḥ
english: Wherever any man caught sight of your son, O Bhārata, there the great chariot-warriors among the warriors turned back.

sanskrit: tān nivṛttān samīkṣyaiva tato 'nye 'pītare janāḥ anyonyaspardhayā rājaṃl lajjayānye 'vatasthire
english: Seeing those turn back, the other men too then took their stand—some out of rivalry with one another, O king, and others out of shame.

sanskrit: punarāvartatāṃ teṣāṃ vega āsīd viśāṃ pate pūryataḥ sāgarasyeva candrasyodayanaṃ prati
english: As they returned, their onrush was such, O lord of peoples, as is the swelling of the ocean at the rising of the moon.

sanskrit: saṃnivṛttāṃs tatas tāṃs tu dṛṣṭvā rājā suyodhanaḥ abravīt tvarito gatvā bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then King Suyodhana, seeing them rallied, went in haste to Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu, and spoke these words.

sanskrit: pitāmaha nibodhedaṃ yat tvā vakṣyāmi bhārata nānurūpam ahaṃ manye tvayi jīvati kaurava
english: Grandsire, mark what I shall say to you, O Bhārata. I deem it unbecoming, O Kaurava, while you yet live—

sanskrit: droṇe cāstravidāṃ śreṣṭhe saputre sasuhṛjjane kṛpe caiva maheṣvāse dravatīyaṃ varūthinī
english: and while Droṇa, foremost of those skilled in arms, lives with his son and his friends, and Kṛpa the mighty archer—that this army of ours should flee.

sanskrit: na pāṇḍavāḥ pratibalās tava rājan kathaṃ cana tathā droṇasya saṃgrāme drauṇeś caiva kṛpasya ca
english: The Pāṇḍavas are in no way a match for you, O king, nor in battle for Droṇa, nor for Droṇa's son, nor for Kṛpa.

sanskrit: anugrāhyāḥ pāṇḍusutā nūnaṃ tava pitāmaha yathemāṃ kṣamase vīra vadhyamānāṃ varūthinīm
english: Surely the sons of Pāṇḍu are objects of your favor, O grandsire, since you suffer, O hero, this army to be slaughtered.

sanskrit: so 'smi vācyas tvayā rājan pūrvam eva samāgame na yotsye pāṇḍavān saṃkhye nāpi pārṣatasātyakī
english: You should have told me, O king, even before the encounter: 'I will not fight the Pāṇḍavas in battle, nor the son of Pṛṣata, nor Sātyaki.'

sanskrit: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tubhyam ācāryasya kṛpasya ca karṇena sahitaḥ kṛtyaṃ cintayānas tadaiva hi
english: Hearing such a word from you, from the preceptor, and from Kṛpa, I should then and there, together with Karṇa, have pondered what was to be done.

sanskrit: yadi nāhaṃ parityājyo yuvābhyām iha saṃyuge vikrameṇānurūpeṇa yudhyetāṃ puruṣarṣabhau
english: If I am not to be forsaken by you two here in the battle, then fight, O bulls among men, with prowess befitting you.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vaco bhīṣmaḥ prahasan vai muhur muhuḥ abravīt tanayaṃ tubhyaṃ krodhād udvṛtya cakṣuṣī
english: Hearing these words, Bhīṣma, laughing again and again, his eyes rolling with anger, spoke to your son.

sanskrit: bahuśo hi mayā rājaṃs tathyam uktaṃ hitaṃ vacaḥ ajeyāḥ pāṇḍavā yuddhe devair api savāsavaiḥ
english: Many a time, O king, have I spoken to you the truthful and salutary word: the Pāṇḍavas are unconquerable in battle, even by the gods together with Vāsava.

sanskrit: yat tu śakyaṃ mayā kartuṃ vṛddhenādya nṛpottama kariṣyāmi yathāśakti prekṣedānīṃ sabāndhavaḥ
english: Yet what I, an old man, am able to do this day, O best of kings, I shall do to the utmost of my power. Behold it now with your kinsmen.

sanskrit: adya pāṇḍusutān sarvān sasainyān saha bandhubhiḥ miṣato vārayiṣyāmi sarvalokasya paśyataḥ
english: This day, before the eyes of all, I shall hold back all the sons of Pāṇḍu, with their troops and their kinsmen, while the whole world looks on.

sanskrit: evam ukte tu bhīṣmeṇa putrās tava janeśvara dadhmuḥ śaṅkhān mudā yuktā bherīś ca jaghnire bhṛśam
english: When Bhīṣma had thus spoken, O lord of men, your sons, filled with joy, blew their conches and beat their drums loudly.
